I realize this film is supposed to be some kind of horror/comedy/satire I guess (I didn't laugh), but what was the deal with the people all hallucinating? Were they all just deranged? Were these ghosts haunting the main characters? Or were the ghosts manifestations of their inner angsts ... or something else?

Um, help?
Hmm, I haven't seen this yet but am looking forward to it. Have you seen other Cronenberg films? He deals a lot in grotesqueness and perceptions of reality. Maybe that plays into it?

I've seen a number of his films.Thinking a bit more, I think the 'ghosts' are the physical manifestations of the character's angst and disturbed minds. It's a plot device, basically, to allow the inner turmoil of a character to come forward. Otherwise it would be hard to convey these conflicts. Sort of like Macbeth when he sees the ghost at the feast - is it a ghost? or a guilt-induced apparition? Or does it matter to Macbeth, since he can't tell either way?

But there's still a great deal of this film, that I don't get. I'm going to be thinking about this for a while.
Of course they were all deranged. The movie is set in Hollywood.

Yes, I agree. I digress a bit but I felt pity for Agatha, the main character. She's treated like a deranged villian by the other characters, but she's really the victim of an incredibly evil environment. And she is considered "ill" while all the other characters are considered "healthy". Edit: Also there's a cameo by Carrie Fischer, as herself. Her mental health and substance abuse issues, she has admitted openly, are a direct result of her Hollywood upbringing and experience. I realize now seeing her early in the film, is an allusion to her books and their message, a message that Cronenberg repeats as a filmmaker.

Ctrl+Alt+[F1-F12] to switch between virtual consoles on a lot of distros.

Besides the really basic ones ('alt + F4', 'alt + tab', etc.), the ones I use the most are:

  • ctrl + alt + arrows: switch workspace in Linux.
  • ctrl + alt + shift + arrows: move current window to a different workspace in Linux.
  • ctrl + pgup: move 1 tab left in Firefox.
  • ctrl + pgdn: move 1 tab right in Firefox.
  • F12: developers tools in Firefox. I like seeing how webpages work.

On Windows, [Ctrl]+[Shift]+[Esc] brings up the task manager.
